title: 'I'm staying, so is the curry': Krishnamoorthi hits back at 'go home' jibe
excerpt: U.S. Rep. Raja Krishnamoorthi answered Palm Bay councilman Chandler Langevin's 'take your curry and go home' post by calling America his home and refusing to let anyone decide who belongs in the country.
body:
• Palm Bay councilman Chandler Langevin told Rep. Raja Krishnamoorthi to "take your curry and go home" in a September 11 post on X.
  • Krishnamoorthi answered: "I'm staying. So is the curry. America is my home."
  • The exchange followed Krishnamoorthi's criticism of a Department of Homeland Security social post targeting "Mr. Singh."
  • Langevin was censured by his own council in October 2025 over anti-Indian remarks; his First Amendment suit against the city settled for $55,000 in February 2026.

WASHINGTON — U.S. Representative Raja Krishnamoorthi has answered the Florida city councilman who told him to “take your curry and go home” — with a one-line rebuke that has become the latest flashpoint in a year-long dispute between the two men.

Krishnamoorthi, an Illinois Democrat and one of the most prominent Indian-origin lawmakers in Congress, responded this week after Palm Bay City Councilman Chandler Langevin wrote on X: “I won Rajesh. Take your curry and go home.”

“I’m staying. So is the curry. America is my home,” Krishnamoorthi shot back. “No bigot gets to decide who is American, who belongs here, or what they have for dinner. That’s the America I’ll always fight for.”

“I’m staying. So is the curry. America is my home. No bigot gets to decide who is American, who belongs here, or what they have for dinner.”

— Raja Krishnamoorthi, U.S. Representative (D-Illinois)

The trigger: a DHS “Mr. Singh” post

The exchange came days after Krishnamoorthi, on September 10, condemned a Department of Homeland Security social media post styled as a movie poster featuring a man identified as “Mr. Singh.” The post told the man to “get off our roads” and warned him to “self-deport or find out,” according to The Times of India. Krishnamoorthi said the post demonized a name shared by more than 160,000 Americans and that Sikh and South Asian Americans were “as American as anyone.”

https://x.com/CongressmanRaja/status/2100212919346569721

Langevin’s reply arrived on September 11. Three days later, he replied again, calling the post a “banger” and asking whether Krishnamoorthi remembered it, according to local Florida reporting. He has used “Rajesh” — a reference to a character on the sitcom The Big Bang Theory — as an epithet for the congressman since October 2025.

A pattern that predates the exchange

Langevin has been under scrutiny since 2025 for a string of social media posts targeting Indian immigrants. In September 2025 he wrote “Deport every Indian immediately” and, two days later, “There’s not a single Indian that cares about the United States.” In one October 2025 post he called Krishnamoorthi a “foreign occupier,” rendered his name “Unpronounceable” and listed his country of origin as “Tatooine,” the fictional planet from Star Wars.

Krishnamoorthi, who was born in India and raised in Peoria, Illinois, answered that his biography — raised in Illinois and elected by its voters — needed no defense.

The Palm Bay council responded in October 2025, voting 4-1 to ask Governor Ron DeSantis to suspend Langevin from office, and later voting 3-2 to censure him, curtailing his ability to introduce agenda items and serve on city-appointed boards. Langevin sued the city, arguing a First Amendment violation; the case settled in February 2026 for $55,000.

Diaspora angle

The clash lands as a visible test of how elected officials of Indian descent navigate a political climate in which anti-immigrant rhetoric has moved from anonymous accounts to council chambers. For Indian Americans — the community Langevin’s posts have repeatedly targeted — the episode underscores both the hostility some local officials still voice openly and the way representation can answer it: Krishnamoorthi’s retort turned the attack line itself into the headline.

He has made a habit of confronting such posts. Earlier this month he criticized the DHS “Mr. Singh” post, and he recently denounced a social media post by a Texas Republican nominee featuring South Asian students at the University of Texas, saying they were being demonized on the basis of appearance.

What’s next

Langevin remains on the Palm Bay council; the 2025 suspension request to DeSantis did not result in his removal. With the congressman’s reply circulating widely this week, the episode is likely to sharpen scrutiny of Langevin’s next posts — and to keep a local Florida dispute squarely in the national conversation about who gets to claim an American identity.

nri_angle: An Indian-origin U.S. congressman publicly rejects a Florida councilman's 'go home' taunt, turning a recurring anti-Indian attack into a defense of who belongs in America.
